newsitem.title: USA: MARYLAND SAYS REVENUES UP 5.8 PCT IN FISCAL 1997.
newsitem.headline: MARYLAND SAYS REVENUES UP 5.8 PCT IN FISCAL 1997.

text.p: Maryland revenue collections rose 5.8 percent in fiscal 1997, exceeding expectations by $120 million, the state comptroller's office said.
"Early data on fiscal year 1997 revenues reveal a healthy state economy with solid job and income growth and rising construction activity," a statement from Comptroller Louis Goldstein said.
Personal income tax revenues, which account for nearly half of the state's $7.6 billion in 1997 general fund revenues, rose about eight percent in fiscal 1997, which ended on June 30.

"Thanks to a 1.7 percent growth in non-farm payrolls and nearly five percent gain in average wages, personal income tax revenues are expected to exceed estimates by $80 million for fiscal year 1997," the statement said.
Sales and use tax revenues rose to $2 billion, a 4.7 percent gain over fiscal 1996. Corporate income tax revenues rose 5.4 percent for the year, outpacing estimates by almost $26 million.
